problem:
$$
U=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 & -\frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} \\ \frac{2}{\sqrt{5}} & 0 & \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}} \\ 0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}5\sqrt{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,V=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}} & -\frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} \\ \frac{3}{\sqrt{10}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices shown above. Given that $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ find the pseudoinverse ${A}^{+}.$
worked_solution:
If $A=UΣ{V}^{T}$ is a singular value decomposition of $A,$ then the pseudoinverse of $A$ is given by

$$
V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T},
$$

where ${Σ}^{+}$ is the pseudoinverse of $Σ.$

First, notice that

$$
V=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,{Σ}^{+}=\frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}],\,{U}^{T}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5} \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{+} & =V\,{Σ}^{+}\,{U}^{T} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{10}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5} \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5} \\ 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5} \\ -2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 0 \\ 3 & 6 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
